about: Decimal512/Int512 defects (open and fixed) of the Sentio fork, as exposed by the checks in tests/. scripts/check_gate.py reads this file: a failing check that matches an OPEN defect is reported as known-open (quick/full exit 3, release BLOCKED), any other failing check is unexpected (exit 1). An open defect whose checks all pass is stale and fails the gate: mark it fixed with evidence in the same change. Expectations encode the intended semantics; they are never edited to make a binary pass. Entries with status `fixed` stay as regression guards: their checks must pass (a failure is unexpected), and a release needs a PROVEN regression proof (recomputed by the gate: the baseline fails, the candidate passes) for every `fixed` entry that names a `proof`.

defects.title: Decimal512 operand scale-ups (plus, minus, comparisons, division, CAST between scales) wrapped silently when the scaled operand left the Int512 range, because the 512-bit overflow check was a no-op. Production build a394e92fb5d
defects.visible_change: a scale-up of plus/minus/least/greatest/divide that leaves Int512 is computed exactly in 1024 bits and raises DECIMAL_OVERFLOW only if the exact result does not fit; comparisons are decided exactly (never DECIMAL_OVERFLOW); CAST between scales raises DECIMAL_OVERFLOW (the result does not fit); decimal_check_overflow = 0 keeps the unchecked wrap for arithmetic

defects.title: (U)Int512 -> Decimal: Int512 values converted to Decimal256/128/64 were truncated to 256 bits without an overflow error, UInt512 values above the Int512 range converted to Decimal512 wrapped, and scale-ups of Int512 into Decimal512 wrapped. Production build a394e92fb5d

Decimal(154, 154) and precision 154: 10^154 does not fit Int512 (exp10_i512(154) wrapped to a negative number), so every computation that needs it was wrong: printing (0.5 printed as -1.1592...), Float64 conversion, casts to and from scale 0 (1 cast to Decimal(154, 154) stored a wrong value instead of overflowing), Float64 to Decimal(154, 154) (0.5 stored as -0.1703...), comparisons with integers (0.5 < 1 gave 0), plus/minus/divide with scale-154 operands, rounding to whole numbers, avg and isDecimalOverflow. defects.title: rolling upgrade: a distributed GROUP BY over nullable fixed keys of 29..64 bytes (e.g. one Nullable(UInt256), four Nullable(Int64), UInt64 + Nullable(Decimal256)) returns wrong results with duplicate groups while shards run the production build and the candidate, in both coordinator directions (two-level aggregation; with an old coordinator also single-level for some shapes); distributed_aggregation_memory_efficient = 0 does not avoid it
defects.effect: wrong result during a mixed-version window (a key appears twice); homogeneous candidate clusters are correct
affects: mixed clusters of 26.3 prod a394e92fb5d and any candidate with the KeysNullMap fix bae5ba481f3
defects.decision: open (Codex 2026-09-25 11:02Z: correctness blocker, mandatory release check; a release stays BLOCKED while it is open). Cause: the old build packs these keys without a null bitmap (zero-sized KeysNullMap), the fix reserves 8 bytes, so the packed key, its hash and its two-level bucket differ between the builds; the old build's own partial aggregation of these keys is also wrong (KD-KEYSNULLMAP-512), so no candidate-side change can make a mixed query correct: old shards and an old coordinator stay wrong whatever the candidate does, and restoring the old packing would restore the old wrong grouping. Resolution candidate, validated in isolation only (tools/replication/upgrade_topology_check.sh, 2026-09-25, CAND3pre e2d571fd15c8 vs production a394e92fb5d): upgrade by replica group so that no distributed query spans both builds - group B (one replica per shard) is upgraded while group A serves every query; then the application's coordinator endpoint and the shard lists switch to group B together; then group A is upgraded. Group-B-only queries equal the oracle (14/14 with either group-B coordinator); a cross-group replica list with a failover to the old group, and an old coordinator over new shards, both reproduce the wrong nullable-key results (6/6 each); a group-only shard list with a replica down fails closed (14/14 errors, no result). Rules it needs: coordinator and all shards in one version group, no cross-group failover while the groups differ, endpoint and shard lists switched together. This is not a rollout approval: the production topology (replica groups, load balancing, failover, Distributed/remote definitions, application endpoints) has not been mapped against these rules, and the production build's own wrong results for these keys (phase A) persist until the upgrade completes
defects.evidence: evidence/fix_ci_20260925/mixed_groupby_cand2* (runs 1-3 against cluster references), evidence/fix_ci_20260925/upgrade_topology_cand3 (topology validation, verdict PASS), release runs (suite mixed-groupby, oracle cases)

affects: CAND4 e7432cac56f (with the #108607 backport a6ab68509bc); the production build a394e92fb5d, the hotfix cd0d6088c5a and CAND3 758106616eb fail the same query with FILE_DOESNT_EXIST; official 26.8.8.8 is correct
defects.decision: fixed by backporting what upstream 26.3 had and the fork lacked: #107758 (26.3 manual backport of 1c1c0315839 from #98882, merged into 26.3 on 2026-06-17, before the #108607 backport #108663). IndexReadTasks/IndexReadColumns were std::unordered_map, copied into the read pool and iterated independently in getPrewhereActions and getReadTaskColumns, so the PREWHERE readers and actions of the text-index steps could be paired in different orders, and MergeTreeRangeReader executed None-type step actions on its sample block although the runtime skips them; with three indexes equals(a, 'alpha') received a non-String column (gdb: MergeTreeRangeReader::executePrewhereActionsAndFilterColumns). Found by a trees-only fetch of upstream 26.3 and `git log fa3aa24e791..de30904` over the direct-read files: #107758 was the only 26.3 merge there missing from the fork. Correction 2026-09-25 ~16:45Z (kept): the first version of this entry said every 26.3 build recursed; that came from runs capped at TasksMax=512, where ClickHouse could not start its threads and dumped core

defects.title: test environment: clickhouse-test replaces the host name in every test output with 'localhost'; the build host is called 'build', so a test whose output contains the word 'build' fails
defects.effect: 04881_low_cardinality_default_value_needle fails on this host only: its one differing line is the reference with 'build' replaced by 'localhost' (90/90 lines otherwise equal); the product output is correct
affects: the stateless gate on hosts whose name occurs in test outputs (sentio_build: 'build')
defects.decision: fixed in the test environment, test and reference unchanged: the gate's stateless server runs in a container with its own UTS namespace and the host name localhost (tools/isolated_ch.sh CH_ISO_HOST_ISOLATION=container, the run_checks.sh default), and clickhouse-test runs with the LD_PRELOAD library tools/hostname_shim.c, so both report localhost and the runner's substitution changes nothing; isolated_ch.sh refuses when the server's and the runner's host names differ. An LD_PRELOAD for the server alone cannot work (ClickHouse clears LD_PRELOAD and re-executes itself) and unprivileged user namespaces are blocked on this host
defects.evidence: evidence/fix_ci_20260925/hostname_isolation/README.txt (container mode: 04881 OK; real host name: 04881 FAIL on exactly the substituted line), evidence/fix_ci_20260925/release_cand4/04881_hostname_substitution_check.txt (the original attribution)
